name: Srivari Brahmotsavam
significance: The most important annual festival at Tirumala, celebrated to commemorate Lord Brahma's worship of Lord Venkateswara.
key_rituals: Ankurarpanam (Seed Sowing)
Dhwajarohanam (Flag Hoisting)
Garuda Vahana Seva (5th Day)
Rathotsavam (Car Festival)
Chakra Snanam (Sacred Bath)
cultural_highlights: Processions of processional deity (Malayappa Swamy) on golden vehicles
Nada Neerajanam musical concerts
Folk dance troupes performing in Mada Streets

name: Dasara Navaratri Utsavams
significance: Grand celebration of Goddess Kanaka Durga's victory over Mahishasura; attracts millions of pilgrims to Vijayawada.
key_rituals: Daily Alankarams (Sri Bala Tripura Sundari to Rajarajeshwari Devi)
Saraswati Puja (Moola Nakshatram Day)
Teppotsavam (Float Festival in Krishna River on Vijayadashami)
cultural_highlights: Hamsa Vahanam float procession in Krishna River
Traditional Kolatam and classical dance programs on Indrakeeladri

name: Maha Shivaratri Brahmotsavam
significance: Annual 11-day celebration of the divine wedding of Lord Mallikarjuna and Goddess Bhramaramba at Srisailam Jyotirlinga.
key_rituals: Pagalankara (Pagada Alankarana) by Chenchu tribals
Linga Abhishekam during Lingodbhava Kala
Kalyanotsavam (Divine Wedding)
Rathotsavam
cultural_highlights: Chenchu tribal dance rituals and offerings
Jagaran (overnight vigil) devotion

name: Sankranti (Makara Sankranti)
significance: The biggest cultural harvest festival celebrated across rural and urban Andhra Pradesh marking the sun's transition into Capricorn.
key_rituals: Day 1: Bhogi (Bonfire and Bhogi Pallu for children)
Day 2: Makara Sankranti (Muggulu/Rangoli competition and Haridasu visits)
Day 3: Kanuma (Cattle worship and agricultural honors)
Day 4: Mukkanuma (Community feasts)
cultural_highlights: Gangireddu (decorated bull) performances
Kite flying and Gobbemmalu displays
Cockfighting in rural coastal belts
Preparation of Ariselu and traditional sweets

name: Ugadi
significance: Marks the beginning of the new era and Hindu lunar calendar year in Andhra Pradesh.
key_rituals: Preparation and tasting of Ugadi Pachadi (mix of six tastes symbolizing life's emotions)
Panchanga Sravanam (reading of the annual astrological almanac)
Kavi Sammelanam (Poets' meets in cultural centers)
cultural_highlights: Doorways decorated with mango leaves and neem flowers
State-level literary awards presentation

name: Chandanotsavam (Chandana Yatra)
significance: The only day of the year when the sandalwood paste covering Lord Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha is removed, revealing His true form (Nijaroopa).
key_rituals: Nijaroopa Darshanam (12-hour viewing window)
Removal of previous year's Chandanam paste
Application of fresh sandalwood paste (Mundala Chandanam)
cultural_highlights: Lakhs of devotees climb Simhachalam hill for dawn queue lines

name: Ratha Saptami
significance: Celebrates the birthday of Sun God (Surya Bhagavan); celebrated with grandeur at Arasavalli Sun Temple and Tirumala.
key_rituals: One-day Mini-Brahmotsavam at Tirumala (Deity taken on 7 different Vahanams from sunrise to night)
Special Ksheerabhishekam at Arasavalli Sun Temple
Surya Namaskar rituals by ocean coasts
cultural_highlights: Sun ray alignment viewing at Arasavalli sanctum

name: Rottela Panduga
significance: Unique syncretic festival celebrated at Bara Shaheed Dargah in Nellore where people of all religions exchange flatbreads (rotti) to fulfill vows.
key_rituals: Exchanging Roti in Swarnala Cheruvu tank water
Categorized Roti exchanges (Sowbhagya Roti for marriage, Vidya Roti for education, Arogya Roti for health)
Offering prayers at the tombs of 12 Martyrs (Bara Shaheed)
cultural_highlights: Massive secular gathering of Hindu, Muslim, and Christian devotees

name: Flamingo Festival
significance: Eco-tourism festival organized by AP Tourism at Sullurpeta near Pulicat Lake and Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary to celebrate migratory birds.
key_rituals: Bird Watching Expeditions at Pulicat Lagoon & Nelapattu
Environmental Awareness Exhibitions
Boating competitions on Pulicat Lake
cultural_highlights: Cultural music and dance performances showcasing coastal Nellore traditions
Photography contests

name: Visakha Utsav
significance: The official annual cultural and tourism carnival hosted along RK Beach promenade in Visakhapatnam by APTDC.
key_rituals: Carnival Parade along Beach Road
Flower show and Food festival setups
Traditional folk art shows (Dhimsa, Tappeta Gullu, Kolatam)
cultural_highlights: Music concerts by national artists
Water sports demonstrations at Rushikonda
Laser and firework shows over RK Beach

name: Vaikuntha Ekadasi
significance: Auspicious day when the Vaikuntha Dwaram (northern gates of heaven) inside Vishnu temples opens to grant salvation to devotees.
key_rituals: Opening of Vaikuntha Dwaram at 00:00 midnight
Special Abhishekam and Sahasra Namarchana
Mukkoti Ekadasi Procession of Lord Malayappa Swamy on Golden Chariot
cultural_highlights: Lakhs of devotees lining up for northern gate passage
Special floral decorations (Pushpa Alankarana) inside temple sanctum

name: Kotappakonda Prabha Utsavam
significance: Massive folk Shivaratri festival at Trikuta Hill in Palnadu where surrounding villages bring giant illuminated towers (Prabhas).
key_rituals: Bringing towering 60-100 feet decorated wooden Prabhas on bullock carts and tractors
Light illumination displays on Prabha towers at night
Abhishekam to Lord Trikuteswara Swamy
cultural_highlights: Spectacular night illumination of hundreds of Prabha structures along hill slopes
Folk music, Kolatam, and local cultural performances

name: Kanipakam Vinayaka Chavithi Brahmotsavam
significance: A grand 21-day annual celebration of Lord Varasiddhi Vinayaka at Kanipakam well-shrine in Chittoor district.
key_rituals: Gramotsavam and Dhwajarohanam
Daily Vahana Sevas (Siddhi-Buddhi Sametha Vinayaka on Mooshika, Peacock, and Elephant vehicles)
Rathotsavam (Car Festival)
Teppotsavam in Bahuda River
cultural_highlights: Classical music and dance concerts arranged by AP Endowments Dept
Special Modaka and Laddu prasadam distributions

name: Antarvedi Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Kalyanotsavam
occurrence_month: January / February (Magha Suddha Saptami to Ekadasi)
significance: Annual celestial wedding celebration of Lord Narasimha Swamy and Goddess Rajya Lakshmi at the Godavari-ocean confluence.
key_rituals: Kalyanotsavam (Divine Wedding) on Bhishma Ekadasi
Rathotsavam (Grand Chariot Procession)
Chakra Snanam holy dip at Godavari-Sea confluence (Anna Chellela Gattu)
cultural_highlights: Massive beach congregation of pilgrims taking holy dips at the sea confluence
Traditional coastal Andhra carnivals and handloom fairs

name: Sirimanotsavam
significance: Historic folk festival celebrating Goddess Pydivithalli, featuring the chief priest riding suspended atop a 60-foot raised wooden pole (Sirimanu).
key_rituals: Sirimanu Procession (Priest seated on the long pole blessings crowds)
Anjali Ratham (Procession of royal palanquin)
White Elephant (Gaja Ratham) and Chariot procession through Vizianagaram streets
cultural_highlights: Tappeta Gullu folk dance troupes leading the procession
Royal family of Vizianagaram Fort hosting temple traditions

name: Poleramma Jathara (Venkatagiri)
significance: Centuries-old village deity fair celebrated in Venkatagiri town to seek Goddess Poleramma's protection against diseases and epidemics.
key_rituals: Making of clay idol of Goddess Poleramma
Prathistapana and nocturnal offerings
Nimajjanam (Immersion of clay deity in local water body at dawn)
cultural_highlights: Veshalu (devotees dressing up as mythological and folk characters)
Traditional Venkatagiri sari handloom exhibitions during jathara

name: Lepakshi Heritage Festival
significance: State cultural festival organized by AP Tourism at the historic Veerabhadra Temple complex to celebrate Vijayanagara art and dance.
key_rituals: Sound and Light (Son et Lumière) show highlighting Lepakshi history
Classical dance recitals in front of monolithic Nandi and Nagalinga
cultural_highlights: Performances by renowned Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam artists
Crafts fair highlighting Rayalaseema artisans and cuisine

name: Devaragattu Banni Utsavam
significance: Ancient traditional ritual at Neraniki hillock in Kurnool district where villagers engage in a ceremonial stick fight to secure processional idols.
key_rituals: Midnight procession of Mala Malleswara Swamy idols up the hill
Ceremonial stick (Banni) contest between rival groups of surrounding villages
Flame torches (Diviteelu) lighting the hilltop battleground
cultural_highlights: High-energy martial folk spectacle involving thousands of torch-bearing villagers

name: Lumbini Festival
significance: Tourism festival organized by AP Tourism to highlight the rich Buddhist heritage of Andhra Pradesh (Nagarjunakonda, Amaravati, Bojjannakonda).
key_rituals: Buddhist chanting and prayer ceremonies led by international monks
Heritage walks across ancient stupas and rock-cut cave circuits
cultural_highlights: Exhibitions detailing Acharya Nagarjuna's philosophy
International cultural exchange programs and seminars

name: Pelican Festival (Atapaka)
significance: Eco-festival celebrated at Atapaka Bird Sanctuary (Kolleru Lake) to mark the annual nesting season of spot-billed pelicans and painted storks.
key_rituals: Bird Watching Tours on Kolleru Lake boats
Wildlife photography competitions
Community environmental pledge sessions by local wetland villagers
cultural_highlights: Folk art and drama shows raising wetland conservation awareness
